newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 28.

text.p: Two of Mexico's main ports along the northwestern Gulf of Mexico were reported closed on Tuesday, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.
The two Tamaulipas state ports, Tampico and Tuxpan, were shut amid winds from the north in Tampico between 65 and 75 km and waves five to eight feet high.
Further south along the gulf, the port of Veracruz was shut to smaller ships, in addition to La Pesca, El Mezquital, Nautla, Alvarado, Altamira and Rosarito.
A cold front in the Gulf of Mexico is expected to reduce temperatures and bring strong winds to the area in the next 24 hours. The ministry recommended caution in sailing along the western gulf.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Slight clouds along northwest Baja California peninsula, and steady winds hitting maximum velocities of between 10 and 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour).
Winds in Gulf of Tehuantepec from the northeast up to 20 knots (38 km/22 miles per hour) with waves reaching heights between eight and 10 feet high.

Moderate cold front heading southwest expected to intensify and hit the region during the next 24 hours with winds from the north from 25 to 35 knots (47 to 66 km/28 to 39 miles per hour) and waves seven to 10 feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with moderate winds of 20 to 30 km along shores of Quintana Roo and the Yucatan peninsula. Possible light rains.
